messages:
leo: Fresh account + followed the quickstart. after creating org and key, first API call returns 403. console shows org active but the quickstart docs implied "ready to go". anyone?

rachel: can you paste the minimal repro and what key you created (personal/service)?

leo: i made an org via SSO and used the "Create API Key" button in org settings -> service keys. code (Go sample):
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.Config{APIKey: os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")})
resp, err := client.Generate(context.Background(), "Hello")
// err -> status 403, body: {"detail":"workspace requires billing"}
```

onboard-bot: Tip: Organizations created via SSO may not receive trial credits automatically. Visit https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/leo-team/billing to confirm.

leo: i actually clicked through billing and added a card. console now shows "billing active". curl to /v1/health is 200. but my Go quickstart still fails with 403 until i restart my sample app container.

sdk-runner: which SDK version? some older SDKs cache auth failure state in long-running processes and might not revalidate key/org after billing changes.

leo: using redwood-go v0.9.0 in the sample image `redwood/quickstart-go:latest`.

morgan: workaround: restart the process after billing change or explicitly re-initialize the client. Also confirm the container uses the same env var (docker env vs host) and that there's no stale secret mounted.

leo: restarted container and it works now. curious: why did curl show 200 earlier but SDK still returned 403?

rachel: two things: (1) the platform can return 403 for billing and 5xx for transient infra. SDK retry behavior can obscure the original status by returning the last observed error. (2) older SDKs sometimes store a cached auth failure to avoid hashtable lookups on every call; that cache didn't invalidate on billing update.

onboard-bot: We've seen multiple onboarding reports about this pattern. Creating ticket RDW-9002 for docs + CLI hints, RDW-9003 for SDK invalidation on billing change.

leo: small note: quickstart README wording is strong about "create org -> try quickstart" but doesn't mention that SSO orgs might not auto-get trial credits. cost me 12 minutes. maybe add a one-liner in the README and a console modal for SSO org creators.

morgan: agree. also recommend the quickstart sample print the HTTP status and response body on first-call failures rather than swallowing it into a generic error. that would have surfaced the billing detail immediately.

sdk-runner: parity note: Python SDK 0.6.x already stopped caching 4xx failures and surfaces the backend body; Go/Node patches in progress. we'll add a small SDK changelog note and a migration line in the quickstart.

rachel: action items: (1) docs: add SSO/trial caveat and restart note (RDW-9002), (2) SDKs: ensure 4xx not cached and return full error history when retries occur (RDW-9003), (3) quickstart samples: print raw status+body on first failure and detect org billing status via /orgs/:id endpoint to give actionable hint (RDW-9004).

leo: thanks all. fixed after restart and adding billing; hope this helps other new users. closing when tickets are triaged. :white_check_mark:
